_body: This page shows the axis positions.
MACH - the position from the home position
ABS  - the position that the program uses
REL  - the relative counter (display only)
TOGO - the distance to go in this move
ALL  - the four positions together
(OPRT):
ORIGIN - make the counter zero, all axes
PRESET - set the counter to a typed value
PTSPRE - make the parts counter zero
This page shows the program.
The active line is red.
Use the arrow keys and the page keys to move
the view.
(OPRT):
O SRH  - load a typed program number
N SRH  - move to a typed block number
SRH v  - find the typed text, down
SRH ^  - find the typed text, up
REWIND - move to the first line
Use this page to edit the program.
You cannot edit during a program.
Up and Down move the line cursor.
Left and Right move the word cursor.
INSERT  - add the typed words after the word
ALTER   - replace the selected word
DEL.WRD - delete the selected word
ALT.LIN - replace the full line
DEL.LIN - delete the full line
N SRH   - find a typed block number
SRH v ^ - find the typed text
SAVE    - write the file (CAN / EXEC)
CANCEL  - discard the changes
The INSERT, ALTER, and DELETE keys do the same.
Type one block. Then push EXEC or ENTER.
The machine must be on.
The emergency stop must not be active.
The control adds the spaces:
M3S1000 becomes M3 S1000.
CLEAR erases the block list.
This page shows the program, the position,
and the distance to go.
ABS and REL select the type of position.
This page shows the words of the active block.
It also shows the modal G and M codes.
This page shows the next block and the modal
codes. The interpreter reads the program before
the machine moves. Thus it can be further on.
Use this page to start a program at a line.
Type a block number (N100) or a line number.
Then push SEARCH.
The control shows the tool, the spindle, the
feed, the coolant, and the modal codes for
that line.
WARNING: the control does not do the M, S, and
T commands before that line. Set the tool, the
spindle, and the coolant with MDI blocks first.
If you do not, the machine can cause injury
and damage. Then push EXEC.
You cannot start at a line in a subroutine.
This page shows the machine program directory.
RETURN or SELECT opens a folder or loads
a file.
(OPRT):
SELECT - load a file or open a folder
O SRH  - move to a typed program number
NEW    - make a new file
PUNCH  - copy the file to the USB drive
DELETE - delete the file (CAN / EXEC)
REFRSH - read the directory again
This page shows the USB drive.
(OPRT):
SELECT - load a file or open a folder
O SRH  - move to a typed program number
NEW    - make a new file
READ   - copy the file to the machine
DELETE - delete the file (CAN / EXEC)
REFRSH - read the drive again
This page shows the length, the radius, and a
comment for each tool.
WEAR and GEOM select the table.
The machine uses the two values together.
(OPRT):
NO.SRH - move to a typed tool number
MEASUR - type Z and the reference height
INP.C. - copy the relative counter
+INPUT - add the typed value
INPUT  - write the typed value
CLEAR  - make ALL / WEAR / GEOM zero
READ   - read the tool table again
PUNCH  - write the tool table
PROBE opens the tool probe page.
DISPLAY UNITS sets the units on the screen:
MACHINE - the machine units
MM      - millimeters
INCH    - inches
PROGRAM - the units of the program
Type a value, or push INPUT to go to the next
value. The control keeps this setting.
The rotary axes are always in degrees.
This page shows the systems G54 to G59.3.
A star shows the active system.
(OPRT):
NO.SRH - move to a system number (1-9)
MEASUR - type an axis and a value. The
current position becomes that value.
+INPUT - add the typed value
INPUT  - write the typed value
PROBE opens the work probe pages.
This page measures the tool on the tool setter.
The position and the speeds come from the
[TOOLSENSOR] section of the ini file.
Z ZERO HEIGHT is the distance from the sensor
face to your Z zero.
Put the tool in the spindle. Move the tool
above the sensor. Then push Z.PRB (CAN / EXEC).
Use these pages to set a work offset.
OUT   - outside edges and corners
IN    - inside surfaces and corners
ANGLE - the angle of an edge
BOSS  - the center of a boss or a pocket
RIDGE - the center of a ridge or a valley
CAL   - calibrate the stylus on a gauge
In the 3x3 grid, green is the workpiece, red is
the start position, purple is the movement.
The center cell is a Z touch.
Use the arrow keys to select a cell.
The text under the grid is read from the probe
routine itself. It says where to put the probe.
P.SET has the clearances and the feeds.
The control writes to the active system.
WARNING: make sure that the path is clear.
Move the probe to the start. Then push EXEC.
This page has the parameters for all the
cycles: the clearances, the step-off, the probe
feeds, the calibration offset, and the sizes of
the features.
Type a value and push INPUT.
The control keeps these values.
Use this page to look after the machine
configuration files (ini and hal).
DIR    - the configuration directory
USB    - the USB drive, for backups
TEXT   - edit the selected file as lines
FIELDS - edit the selected file as values
INFO   - paths, joints, and the launcher
Select a file in DIR. TEXT and FIELDS both edit
that file. SAVE writes <file>.bak first.
The control must be restarted for a change to
take effect: (OPRT) RESTRT.
EXIT stops the control (CAN / EXEC). Both need the machine OFF.
This page shows the configuration directory.
The selected file is orange with a > mark.
RETURN or SELECT opens a folder or selects
a file and goes to FIELDS (or TEXT).
(OPRT):
SELECT - select the file or open the folder
COPY   - copy the file to the USB drive
RESTOR - put back the .bak copy (CAN / EXEC)
REFRSH - read the directory again
This page shows the USB drive.
(OPRT):
SELECT - select the file or open the folder
COPY   - copy the file to the configuration
directory (CAN / EXEC). The old file
is kept as .bak.
REFRSH - read the drive again
Use this page to edit the file as lines.
USE AN EXTERNAL KEYBOARD: this page keeps
small letters, and Shift and Caps Lock do not
change the page here.
You cannot edit during a program.
Up and Down move the line cursor.
Left and Right move the word cursor.
RETURN adds the typed text as a new line.
The INSERT, ALTER, and DELETE keys act on
the selected word.
A * after the file name shows unsaved changes.
Push [>] for the (OPRT) keys.
(OPRT):
INSERT  - add the typed words after the word
ALTER   - replace the selected word
DEL.WRD - delete the selected word
ALT.LIN - replace the full line
DEL.LIN - delete the full line
SRH v ^ - find the typed text
SAVE    - write the file, old copy to .bak
CANCEL  - discard the changes
(OPRT) page 2:
RESTOR  - put back the .bak copy
RESTRT  - save and restart the control
Use this page to edit the file as values.
USE AN EXTERNAL KEYBOARD (see TEXT).
Type a value, then push INPUT or RETURN.
The orange line shows the full value.
Gray cells are read-only: use TEXT for them.
ini file: one field for each KEY = value.
SEC v ^    - next / previous section
DELETE key - make the value empty
SRH v ^ - find the typed text
SAVE    - write the file, old copy to .bak
CANCEL  - discard the changes
RESTOR / RESTRT - (OPRT) page 2, as TEXT
Push [>] for the hal file fields.
hal file: two fields for each command.
net    - the SIGNAL, then the PINS
setp   - the PIN, then the VALUE
loadrt - the COMP, then the ARGS
addf   - the FUNC, then the THREAD
APPLY - send the setp on this line to the
running hal now (CAN / EXEC).
This does not save the file.
PINS  - show the live values of the pins
on the selected line.
The other keys are the same as for an ini file.
This page shows the ini file, the configuration
directory, the joints and the kinematics, the
selected file and its .bak copy, and whether
the restart launcher (run_gui.sh) is in use.
(OPRT) RESTRT - save and restart the control.
EXIT stops the control (CAN / EXEC). Both need the machine OFF.
This page shows the active alarms in red and
the alarm history.
RESET (ESC) or CLEAR moves the active alarms
to the history. If the cause is still present,
the alarm comes again. Correct the cause.
This page shows the tool path.
Each tool has a different color.
The rapid moves are dim blue.
A completed move becomes gray.
The marker is the tool tip.
The orange line is the A and C tool axis.
Softkeys: the XY, XZ, YZ, and ISO views, ZOOM,
the arrows to move the view, FIT, and REDRAW.
REDRAW erases the gray trace.
Live state of the field devices: EtherCAT
terminals and drives, Modbus / RS485 devices,
other hardware drivers. One row on the left for
each device; its lamp is green when its status
pins (slave online + operational) are all TRUE,
red when not, gray when it has none.
Read-only: nothing here changes HAL.
Arrows    - move the cursor (down the column,
off the end = next device/group)
Touch     - a cell, or a row in the left list
GRP v ^   - next / previous (OPRT)
SRH v ^   - type text, find it in label/pin/tag
HOLD      - freeze the display; counts still run
LOG       - list of changes with times
CLR.CNT   - zero rise/fall counts, min/max, log
REGEN     - (OPRT) page 2: rebuild io_map.yaml
from live HAL, old copy to .bak
Reading a cell:
I / O  - field input / output (PHYS)
lamp   - green = active (after invert)
value  - number for float / s32 / u32 pins
orange outline - changed in the last second
?      - the name is not in HAL (typo, or
the device is not loaded)
Bottom lines: full name, type, direction, the
linked signal, R/F counts, time since change,
min/max. Values are read about 20 times a second;
a shorter pulse can be missed by the lamp - watch
the R/F counts and the LOG.
io_map.yaml (config dir) - edit with DIR > TEXT:
phys: - device: NAME
status: [pin, ...]  all TRUE = green
points:
- {pin: P, tag: T, dir: I, label: L,
desc: D, invert: true,
bits: {0: RDY, 3: FAULT}}
hal:  - group: NAME
points: [...same keys...]
Only pin is needed. bits: shows one lamp for each
named bit of an int word (drive status word).
Edits load the next time PHYS / HAL is opened.
Needs python3-yaml to read the file.
Live state of the internal HAL signals, grouped
by hal file and its section headers, plus the
LINUXCNC and JOINT n groups (enables, homing,
limits, following error, tool change, spindle).
